title: On the convexity of the KdV Hamiltonian
date_note: The versioned arXiv PDF is labelled v1/20 February 2015 but prints March 8, 2022; the downloaded bytes, rather than an assumed typesetting date, are pinned.

main_theorems.label: Theorem 1.1
statement_components: One complex open neighborhood V of the entire nonnegative ell2 action quadrant and an analytic extension of the physical renormalized KdV Hamiltonian to V.
The bilinear Hilbert gradient agrees coordinatewise with the existing KdV frequencies minus 8*pi^3*n^3 on V intersect V0.
Gradient at zero is zero and its full bounded derivative is -6 times identity.
An analytic local diffeomorphism near zero on complex ell2.
One positive radius, chosen before I and J, for the real Hessian bound d2H(I)[J,J] <= -norm(J)^2 on nonnegative ell2 actions, for every real ell2 direction J.
main_theorems.domain: Positive-index actions (I_n) for n >= 1; nonnegative includes zero coordinates; original Hkdv on weighted ell^(3,1)_+.
main_theorems.topology: Norm topology on complex ell2; open ambient extension around every cone point.
remaining: Glue the identified joint endpoint squared-primitive charts across entire gaps and canonical cuts; fill the unsquared endpoint values, handle central endpoints and identify the shared global L2 labels. Prove nonpositivity and gap-scale bounds for actual moments.
Construct physical KdV contour moments and analytic descent on one complex neighborhood of the weighted ell^(-1,1) nonnegative cone (Lemma 4.6(ii)).
Prove locally common complex-neighborhood bounds |8*n*pi*R_n| <= C*|I_n|^2 for those moments.
Identify the analytically summed contour series with physical renormalized energy using the finite-gap trace formula and density.
Identify its bilinear Hilbert gradient with physical KdV frequencies minus 8*pi^3*n^3 on the full common domain.
Prove the KdV quadratic Taylor coefficients giving -6*Id.
Complete positive-index Hessian and real-cone transport for the earlier Coeff-based local concavity adapter.

main_theorems.label: Theorem 1.2
statement_components: For every real s in [-1/2,0] and every finite p >= 2, the same global H^-1 KdV Birkhoff map restricts to a real analytic diffeomorphism from L_0^(s,p) onto ell_0^(s+1/2,p).
main_theorems.domain: Real, mean-zero periodic distributions; two-sided complex sequence coordinates with z_0=0 and z_-n=conj(z_n).
main_theorems.topology: Fourier-Lebesgue and weighted sequence Banach norm topologies; not weak-star endpoints.
remaining: Fourier-Lebesgue spectral asymptotics and analytic restriction
Surjectivity by action reduction, plus inverse regularity

main_theorems.label: Theorem 1.3
statement_components: For every s in [-1/2,0] and every finite p >= 2 the KdV initial value problem is globally C0 well-posed on the real mean-zero Fourier-Lebesgue space L_0^(s,p).
main_theorems.domain: All real initial data in L_0^(s,p), all real times; solutions interpreted through the distributional H^-1 framework referenced by the paper.
main_theorems.topology: Continuity of trajectories and dependence on initial data in the Fourier-Lebesgue norm, compatible with the H^-1 solution notion.
main_theorems.proof_note: Presented in the introduction as an immediate application of Theorem 1.2 and the previously constructed KdV frequency/solution theory; no separately labelled proof later.
remaining: Physical KdV frequency reality and coordinate continuity
Conjugation of sequence phase flow by the same physical KdV Birkhoff map
Agreement/uniqueness with accepted H^-1 distributional solution theory

source_labels: Lemma 4.6 contour bound and analytic integration step
contour_calculus_progress.normalization: counterclockwise contours; I=-(1/pi)*integral F_n, R=(1/pi)*integral F_n^3; coefficients 8*n^3*pi^3 and 8*n*pi
contour_calculus_progress.explicit_quadratic_constant: 16*pi*B*A^3*K^2 when radius <= B*gamma, |F| <= A*gamma/n, gamma^2/n <= K*|I|
contour_calculus_progress.remaining: Integrate the constructed actual unordered high pairs with complete globally ordered Hill labels and central contours; prove real spectral ordering and primitive endpoint values; continue across actual gap cuts; identify the rough Hill/action data; prove uniform complex gap/action bounds and action descent; identify physical high-energy expansion (4.7).

physical_coefficient_progress.source: Physical energy coefficient needed for Lemma 4.4 / (4.7), p. 28
physical_coefficient_progress.specialization: Existing physical NLS hierarchy at a=-1, b=-q
physical_coefficient_progress.domains: Smooth period-one complex q, mean zero for the assembled first-five coefficients and trace estimate; real energy correspondence also proved.
physical_coefficient_progress.physical_hill_ode: -y_second_derivative + q*y = z^2*y for actual constructed scalar solutions
physical_coefficient_progress.initial_data: All scalar position/derivative vectors, including spectral parameter z=0
physical_coefficient_progress.trace_error: For every natural N, exists C>0 before all real |r|>=1, error <= C/(2*|r|)^(N+5), with the physical higher Hamiltonian tail retained.
physical_coefficient_progress.remaining: Continue the free-normalized source primitive to the canonical finite-gap cut complement, construct its exterior squared expansion and normalized analytic inversion remainder, then apply the existing generic Hamiltonian Laurent identification. The actual cosh trace identity is proved on the current continuation domain.

local_spectral_progress.potential_space: C([0,1], C), with its sup Banach norm
local_spectral_progress.matching: The local squared primitive agrees with the square of every sufficiently small normalized branch satisfying 2*cosh(F)=sigma*Delta, sigma^2=1.

source_continuation_progress.domain: Energy in the complex slit plane; Delta(lambda,s*q)^2-4 nonzero for every real s in [0,1].
source_continuation_progress.continued_root_conjugation: r(conj(lambda),q)=-conj(r(lambda,q)) on the admissible source domain at real continuous q.
source_continuation_progress.continued_primitive_conjugation: F(conj(lambda),q)=-conj(F(lambda,q)) on the admissible source domain at real continuous q.
source_continuation_progress.high_shifted_primitive_uniform_imaginary: |Im(F(z^2,q)+i*n*pi)|<pi/2 at all admissible high-disc points on a common complex potential neighborhood.

high_contour_progress.potential_topology: Sup-norm Banach space C([0,1], C), allowing complex perturbations.
high_contour_progress.high_contour_family: Image under lambda=z^2 of the counterclockwise circle C(n*pi,pi/4), n>N.
high_contour_progress.quantifiers: For every q, exists N>0 and complex open V containing q, before every a in V and every n>N. All source potentials s*a with 0<=s<=1 avoid the actual branch locus on those contours.

high_energy_pair_progress.potential_space: C([0,1], C), with complex sup-norm topology
high_energy_pair_progress.energy_region: Image of B(n*pi,pi/4) under lambda=z^2, for positive high indices
high_energy_pair_progress.endpoint_trace_levels: Both Delta values equal 2 for even n and -2 for odd n
high_energy_pair_progress.analytic_energy_midpoint: m^2+g/4=(l+r)/2, using intrinsic frequency midpoint m and squared gap g
high_energy_pair_progress.reality_scope: Real continuous potentials only; actual Green identity for any unit-modulus Floquet multiplier.
high_energy_pair_progress.endpoint_limit_scope: At every actual high radicand zero, for real continuous potentials on a common complex neighborhood and cutoff, from both nonreal energy half-planes; no simplicity assumed. Literal values at excluded branch points not asserted.

primitive_sheet_progress.potential_space: C([0,1], C), real-valued locus, no norm smallness assumption
primitive_sheet_progress.proof_method: Actual scalar IVP conjugation, Green identity, connected real source continuation and free anchoring.

high_endpoint_progress.potential_space: C([0,1], C), real-valued locus, common complex potential neighborhood
high_endpoint_progress.joint_squared_primitive_matching_scope: Local open joint charts at every high branch point, agreeing with actual F_n^2 on admissible parameters of the high energy region; no entire-gap gluing yet.
